B3.topic: 腦子不配合的時候真的有效的專注方法

claims.label: Phone on desk vs. in another room (Experiment 1)
claims.what_it_means: In a 520-person experiment, simply having your own phone on the desk (vs. in another room) significantly lowered working-memory task (OSpan) performance, even though people weren't consciously thinking about the phone.

source.title: Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One’s Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity
source.venue: Journal of the Association for Consumer Research
source.verbatim: Phone Location significantly affected both OSpan performance (F(2, 514) 5 3.74, p 5 .02, partial h2 5 .014) and RSPM score (F(2, 514) 5 3.96, p 5 .02, partial h2 5 .015).
source.note: Publisher page (journals.uchicago.edu) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; verbatim text confirmed against a full-text PDF mirror of the same published article. DOI/title/authors independently verified via Crossref.

claims.label: Phone on desk vs. in another room (Experiment 2, replication)
claims.what_it_means: In a second, independent 275-person experiment replicating Experiment 1, working-memory capacity (OSpan) again dropped significantly as phone location moved from 'other room' to 'desk' — and the effect was larger for people who scored higher on smartphone dependence.

source.title: Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One’s Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity
source.venue: Journal of the Association for Consumer Research
source.verbatim: A 3 (Phone Location: desk, pocket/bag, other room) × 2 (Phone Power: on, off) between-subjects ANOVA revealed a significant effect of Location on OSpan performance (F(2, 263) 5 3.53, p 5 .03, partial h2 5 .026).
source.note: Same access caveat as c1: publisher page 403'd automated fetch; verbatim confirmed via full-text PDF mirror of the same article. DOI/title/authors independently verified via Crossref.

B4.topic: 不用建一套系統也有效的生產力方法

claims.label: Implementation intentions (if-then plans) meta-analysis, general goal attainment
claims.what_it_means: Across 94 independent tests, people who wrote a specific 'if situation Y happens, I will do X' plan for a goal were substantially more likely to attain that goal than people with only a general intention — no habit-tracking system, just one sentence written in advance.

source.title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta‐analysis of Effects and Processes
source.venue: Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, Vol. 38
source.verbatim: Findings from 94 independent tests showed that implementation intentions had a positive effect of medium-to-large magnitude (d= .65) on goal attainment.

claims.label: Implementation intentions for physical activity, post-intervention
claims.what_it_means: Across 26 studies on getting people to actually exercise, those who formed a specific if-then plan (e.g., 'if it's 7am on Monday, I will go for a run') showed a small-to-medium boost in physical activity right after the intervention, compared to people who didn't plan this way.

source.title: A meta-analytic review of the effect of implementation intentions on physical activity
source.verbatim: The overall effect size of implementation intentions was 0.31, 95% confidence intervals (CI) [0.11, 0.51] at post-intervention and 0.24, 95% CI [0.13, 0.35] at follow-up.
source.note: Verbatim confirmed on a third-party research-summary page (McMaster Optimal Aging Portal) reproducing the published abstract, since the publisher (tandfonline.com) 403'd automated fetch. DOI/title independently verified via Crossref.

claims.label: Implementation intentions for goal attainment, clinical/analogue mental-health samples
claims.what_it_means: Across 28 experimental comparisons (excluding one outlying very large effect) involving people with diagnosed or sub-clinical mental health difficulties, forming a simple if-then plan produced a large improvement in whether they actually achieved their goal.

source.title: Does forming implementation intentions help people with mental health problems to achieve goals? A meta‐analysis of experimental studies with clinical and analogue samples
source.verbatim: Excluding one outlying (very large) effect, forming implementation intentions had a large effect on goal attainment (d+ = 0.99, k = 28, N = 1,636).
source.note: This effect size is specific to clinical/analogue (mental-health) samples, not the general population — keep that scope in the narration if used.
